newsitem.title: USA: Rohm and Haas rises after favorable reports.
newsitem.headline: Rohm and Haas rises after favorable reports.

text.p: Rohm and Haas Co shares were sharply higher Monday after two analysts issued reports on improving prospects at the firm.
Late in the session, shares were up 1-1/4 to 65-1/2, after trading as high as 66-5/8.
Merrill Lynch analyst Frank Mitsch said in a report Monday positive volume and materials trends would aid earnings at Rohm and Haas.

"We expect the company to report significantly up earnings for (third quarter 1996)," Mitsch said. "While our estimate for 35 percent growth in the third quarter my or may not prove to be too optimistic, we anticipate that earnings will exceed the $1.07 (per share) consensus estimates."

On Friday, PaineWebber analyst Paul Raman issued a note saying he had seen "positive developments" in a recent meeting with Rohm and Haas management, but he did not change his neutral rating or earnings estimates.
"The prospects for their earnings look pretty good going forward," Raman told Reuters. "There's quite a few good things going on at the company."
Raman said lower materials costs in its AtoHaas acrylic sheet venture in Europe held out the prospect that this loss- making business might reach a break-even point.
He also said the water-based polymers business was strong, and the ion-exchange business also was beginning to improve.
Rohm and Haas spokeswoman Laura Hadden said the company knew of no reason behind the share price increase.
"The company has not made any announcements today, nor do we plan to," Hadden said.
"We're happy to see it (the increase). We've been thinking our stock's been undervalued for some time," she said.
